correctness.rationale: The exact claim concerns one completely specified finite complex. Direct and columnwise enumeration both produce 2,401 augmented faces; a deterministic complete 1,178-pair matching has acyclic orientation of all 9,220 Hasse incidences. Three critical dimension-three and 42 critical dimension-four cells remain. Every one of 126 integer Morse attaching coefficients vanishes. The three-skeleton is a wedge of three 3-spheres and its third Hurewicz map is an isomorphism, so all 42 four-cell attaching maps are nullhomotopic. Three constructed integral 3-cycles have zero original signed boundaries and are certified to be an integral basis. All 24 row and 120 column permutations were applied directly to oriented cycles; a determinant-minus-one basis gives the perfect-pairing permutation action and column-sign twist. The complete 35-class Lefschetz character and independently checked symmetric-group character orthogonality prove the rational H4 decomposition. Code and expected output are separately packaged and replayed.

value.rationale: The integral row-pairing permutation lattice of rank three, twisted by the full column sign character, records nontrivial finite-symmetry structure not determined by the known nonequivariant ranks, their duals, or any rational character alone. It realizes the natural S4→S3 action on pair partitions and is certified by an explicit unimodular basis rather than a change of coefficients. The balanced small four-row multiple chessboard complex is a natural case of the emerging higher-row theory, and its low-degree integral module is a meaningful precise invariant useful in equivariant configuration-space questions. The 42-dimensional multiplicity-free rational Specht decomposition provides the complementary character benchmark; no general theorem is required for the concrete symmetry result.
